first_impression.reaction: My assistant flagged it, so I gave it the first screen. It reads nicely and it isn't selling at me, which I appreciate. But 'it works for 40 guests as well as 200' tells me straight away this wasn't written with a 350-guest wedding in mind. My assistant can skim the rest for anything about scale or privacy; I would not read it myself.

journey.quote: It suits couples who want the entrance to the reception to feel considered, and it works for 40 guests as well as 200.
journey.reaction: The tone is right, calm and not gushing. The number is the issue. 200 is where my list starts, not where it stops. Naming a ceiling makes me wonder whether anyone here has done a room my size.

journey.quote: At a destination venue, confirm space, setup times, weather rules and power before you commit to a style.
journey.reaction: Sensible and short. This is the kind of line my assistant would actually pass on.

journey.quote: Have a few glasses of something without alcohol ready too.
journey.reaction: For half my family the non-alcoholic option is not an afterthought, it is the welcome drink. 'A few glasses' reads as if the writer has only pictured one kind of guest list.

journey.section: A Personal Touch with Photos and a Message
journey.quote: For a smaller wedding, a photograph of each guest with a short handwritten note and their table number is hard to beat for warmth.
journey.reaction: Lovely, not for us. Several ideas here are clearly sized for something much smaller. That's fine, it just confirms the article isn't for me.

journey.section: A Screen or QR Lookup on Arrival
journey.quote: It handles a large guest list well and is the easiest style to change at the last minute.
journey.reaction: This is the one idea that fits our size. But nobody mentions who can see the full guest list behind a code. If our list ends up on a phone outside the venue, that's a leak. I'd expect a planner to raise that before I do.

journey.section: A Seating Wall of Photos or Cards
journey.quote: It holds a lot of names and reads well from a distance.
journey.reaction: Fine, but our guests' full names on an open wall is something every phone in the room can photograph. Again, nothing on discretion.

journey.quote: Queensland guidance for events is a sound reference here.
journey.reaction: Why am I reading a Queensland government PDF? The two paragraphs after it are a lot of detail for something our planner and the venue's staff would simply take care of. This is where it starts over-explaining.

journey.section: Interactive Seating Charts at a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Who sets up the display and who packs it down?
journey.reaction: The venue questions are the most useful part for us. My assistant would keep this list. I'd add closing the property and security to it myself.

journey.section: Interactive Seating Charts at a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so these answers are settled before the design is.
journey.reaction: Good. In writing is what I want to hear. 'Inclusions' sounds a little like a package, though.

journey.section: Plan It with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Advisor works in your time zone and plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: One contact who works in Dubai hours is genuinely relevant. But nothing tells me they have handled 300-plus guests, VIP arrivals or a private security team. That is what I'd need before my assistant picks up the phone.

unanswered_questions: Has the Wedded Concierge team delivered weddings of 200 to 400 guests, and can they show that privately?
How is our guest list kept private, including anything behind a QR code or screen, and who on the team or at the venue sees it?
Can the team work alongside our own security team and the venue's, including at the entrance where the seating display stands?
Can the destination venues they work with be taken for exclusive use over several days?
Is there a private or referral route to enquire, rather than a general form?

turn_offs_found.quote: The guide also asks for open, flat, clear pathways to entrances and exits with nothing in the way.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. Two paragraphs of government guidance is detail my planner should own, not something I need explained to me.

turn_offs_found.quote: Wind lifts paper cards, sun glares off mirrors and glass, rain ruins ink and heat wilts flowers and softens chocolate.
turn_offs_found.why: Reads as a checklist for a couple doing it themselves. At my level I assume someone else has thought of this.

would_share_with: My assistant, for the venue question list only

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk it through, start a conversation with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: Not from a blog post about escort cards. I'd only enquire through a referral or a private introduction, and nothing here shows they work at my scale or how they handle privacy. My assistant might note the name for later.

top_3_changes: Remove the guest-number ceiling from the intro. Old: "and it works for 40 guests as well as 200." New: "and it works for an intimate dinner as well as a very large reception."

Raise guest-list discretion in the digital lookup section. Old: "Keep a printed list nearby and a person who knows the plan." New: "Keep a printed list nearby and a person who knows the plan, and decide in advance who should be able to see the full guest list behind the code or screen."

Treat the non-alcoholic welcome as equal, not an extra. Old: "Have a few glasses of something without alcohol ready too." New: "Offer something without alcohol alongside the champagne, or in its place, depending on your guests."

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant reads first, private-channel enquirer)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Suggested edits use exact old strings, add no new facts or measurements, and stay out of fees, commissions and supplier sourcing or vetting
HTML comments and image slots ignored as a real reader would

open_questions.question: This is a how-to idea post aimed broadly; should UHNW low relevance be weighted down for this topic rather than driving rewrites?

assumptions: Persona card is provisional and uncalibrated; reactions reflect the card as written.
Read in fast mode: first screen in full, then the assistant's skim of the rest as the persona would realistically encounter it.
